assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology, from proglucagon processing and the insulinotropic action of GLP-1(7-36) to degradation-resistant long-acting agonists, produced a new class of drugs for type 2 diabetes and obesity with cardiovascular and renal benefit. The change in medicine and in the understanding of gut-brain-pancreas physiology is large and clearly discernible.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiology and secretion of GLP-1), Drucker (intestinotrophic and pleiotropic actions, translational work) and Knudsen (design of liraglutide and semaglutide) cover discovery, mechanism and drug. Mojsov's contribution to peptide identification and Habener's role (not in the credited list) make the allocation contested; the three-person limit forces a choice.
assessment.maturity: Over three decades of basic work and more than a decade of large outcome trials and widespread clinical use. Confirmation is extensive and independent; timing is very mature, arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Credit for the original identification of the active GLP-1 peptide is disputed and I have not independently verified details.
Whether the prize should reward physiology or the drug development track, or both, is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells with chimeric antigen receptors turned adoptive immunotherapy into a reproducible treatment that induces durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies. This is a clear conceptual and clinical shift in cancer treatment.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (early costimulatory CAR design), June (clinical translation of CD19 CAR-T) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell transfer and early CAR trials) form a plausible trio. Eshhar and other early CAR pioneers are not in the credited names, which leaves a fairness question I cannot resolve here.
assessment.maturity: Several approved products and over a decade of follow-up with independent confirmation. Solid-tumor translation remains limited, and long-term safety is still being defined.
uncertainties: Early CAR concept credit beyond the listed names is a risk for the prize configuration.
Durability and safety data for secondary malignancies continue to accrue.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined a new form of organelle-to-nucleus signalling (IRE1, HAC1/XBP1 splicing, then PERK and ATF6 arms) and a basic principle of proteostasis with links to diabetes, neurodegeneration and cancer. Originality and conceptual clarity are high.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori made the decisive mechanistic discoveries (IRE1 as the sensor, the HAC1 splicing and the UPR element). The pair gives a clean configuration, though others such as Kaufman, Ron and Shamu contributed to branches of the pathway.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism has been confirmed repeatedly over 30 years and is textbook. Therapeutic exploitation is still emerging, but the discovery stands without it.
uncertainties: Whether Ron and others on the PERK/ISR arm should share credit is a judgment call I cannot verify from the supplied text.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics enables millisecond-precise control of defined cell types and has transformed causal neuroscience, with clinical extensions in vision restoration. The tool-driven change in the field is large and quickly recognised.
assessment.attribution: Microbial rhodopsin channel discovery (Nagel, Hegemann, with Bamberg) and its adaptation to neurons (Boyden, Deisseroth, and Miesenböck's earlier genetic photoactivation) leave six plausible names for at most three seats, so allocation is the main difficulty.
assessment.maturity: Widely replicated and used in thousands of studies. Clinical impact is limited so far. Recognition is mature on the methods side.
uncertainties: Substantial allocation dispute among at least six contributors.
Prize in this category favours discoveries about physiology or medicine; a research tool may be judged on its enabled discoveries.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Orexin/hypocretin identified the neuropeptide system lost in narcolepsy type 1 and explained a major sleep disorder, and led to orexin receptor antagonists as insomnia drugs. The conceptual clarity and medical relevance are strong.
assessment.attribution: Two groups (Sakurai/Yanagisawa and de Lecea/Kilduff) discovered the peptides independently in 1998, while Mignot's canine genetics of the receptor and the human orexin loss tie the discovery to disease. Fair allocation among five names is difficult.
assessment.maturity: More than 25 years since discovery with strong independent confirmation and approved drugs. Timing is mature.
uncertainties: Priority between the two 1998 discoveries and the treatment of Mignot's disease link are contentious.
I cannot verify exact contributions of each credited person.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Wnt/Int1 discovery as a proto-oncogene in mouse mammary tumours connected to Drosophila wingless, and the elaboration of a signalling pathway central to development, stem cells and cancer. Foundational and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Nusse and Varmus identified Int1 and established the Wnt link; the later receptor, beta-catenin and Drosophila genetics involved many other groups outside the credited names. Varmus already holds a Nobel Prize, which raises a policy question.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature and confirmed in many contexts. Direct therapeutic payoff remains modest, though the biology is firmly established.
uncertainties: Varmus's earlier Nobel Prize may weigh against a repeat laureate.
Credit for pathway elucidation beyond Int1 is distributed across many labs.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TOR and mTOR as the central regulator of cell growth and nutrient sensing; the discovery connected rapamycin to a conserved kinase pathway relevant to cancer, ageing, metabolism and immunosuppression.
assessment.attribution: Hall discovered TOR in yeast and is the central figure; Sabatini identified mammalian mTOR and mTORC1 regulation. Schreiber's role in FKBP12-rapamycin chemistry is real but different in kind. Brown and Abraham, not credited, also identified mTOR.
assessment.maturity: Extensively confirmed over 30 years with clinical use of rapalogs. Timing is mature.
uncertainties: Omission of Brown/Abraham from the credited names complicates fairness.
Sabatini's allocation may be affected by non-scientific considerations I cannot assess.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: High-frequency deep brain stimulation of the subthalamic nucleus and thalamus transformed treatment of advanced Parkinson's disease and opened circuit-based neuromodulation for other disorders. Clinical impact is large.
assessment.attribution: Benabid's decisive 1987 observation and development of chronic high-frequency stimulation is clear; DeLong's pathophysiological model (not credited here) was pivotal and a prize without it would be incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Over 30 years of use and randomised trial confirmation. Recognition is timely or overdue, though the prize category emphasises a mechanistic discovery and mechanism of action remains debated.
uncertainties: Mechanism of DBS is incompletely understood.
Credit configuration without DeLong or Wichmann is uncertain.
